turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“I’m here for my annual well-check, but I also have a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. It doesn’t hurt and there’s no tenderness.”
How long has this rough, scaly patch been
“About a few months now—it’s been slowly staying about the same, and it still doesn’t hurt or feel tender.”
Have you noticed any bleeding, ulceration, or rapid growth
“Since I’ve noticed it, I haven’t had any bleeding or ulceration, and it hasn’t been rapidly growing—just a slow, steady plaque on the back of my left hand.”
Have you had a lot of sun exposure over your lifetime, or do you have a personal or family history of skin cancer?
“I’ve had a fair amount of sun exposure over the years—I enjoy walking outside and sunbathing—but I don’t recall any personal history of skin cancer, and there’s no known family history either.”
